title: DoT and C-DOT Sign Agreement to Establish End-to-End Optical Network Testbed for Indigenous Optical Communication Technologies
subtitle: Testbed to bridge the gap between lab-stage innovation and market readiness through testing and validation of indigenous optical communication technologies
body_text:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, has officially signed a strategic five-year agreement with the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) to establish a state-of-the-art End-to-End Optical Network Test Bed. Funded and supported by DoT, this Test Bed will be located at the C-DOT Campus in New Delhi. It will serve as a critical real-world environment to accelerate the development, testing, and commercialization of optical communication solutions created by Indian startups and industry players.
The agreement was signed on 27th August 2026 by the representatives of DoT & C-DOT in the august presence of Sh. Alok Shukla, Advisor (Technology), DoT; Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT and Sh. Atul Kumar Singh, DDG (Networks & Technologies), DoT.
Empowering India’s Optical Communication Ecosystem
The public-funded project primarily bridges the gap between lab-stage innovation and market readiness. This initiative will further accelerate the development and deployment of home-grown optical communication technologies, to further advance the vision of “Aatmanirbhar Bharat” and strengthen India’s capabilities in next-generation communication infrastructure. By combining C-DOT’s mature, field-ready products across optical core, access, and Quantum Security technologies, the test bed will function as a catalyst for the Indian telecom ecosystem.
The Test Bed will serve as a platform for skill development and capacity building in advanced optical communications, providing students, researchers, startups and industry professionals opportunities for hands-on training and exposure to next-generation optical networking technologies.
The End-to-End Optical Network Test Bed will be a shared national resource for innovation, testing, validation, skill development and commercialization. The technical blueprint structures the initiative into two definitive phases:
• Set-up Phase (Years 1–2): Focuses on creating the necessary infrastructure for the Test Bed, including the various elements of Optical Core, Optical Access as well as Quantum Security besides third party advanced test & measurement tools from trusted vendors, resulting in the formal rollout of the test bed.
• Operations & Maintenance Phase (Years 3–5): Dedicated to sustained test bed maintenance, direct technical support for ecosystem users, and targeted educational outreach programs.
About the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT)
C-DOT is a premier telecom technology research and development center of the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India. It has consistently been at the forefront of developing indigenous, secure, standards-compliant and deployment-ready telecom technologies, aligned with the national priorities of technological self-reliance and secure digital infrastructure.

enrichment.summary: DoT and C-DOT signed a five-year agreement on 27 August 2026 to establish an End-to-End Optical Network Test Bed at C-DOT's New Delhi campus. The DoT-funded facility will test and validate indigenous optical communication technologies developed by Indian startups and industry, bridging the gap between lab research and market-ready products. The project runs in two phases: infrastructure Set-up (Years 1-2) and Operations & Maintenance (Years 3-5), covering Optical Core, Optical Access and Quantum Security technologies.
enrichment.context:
India's telecom sector has been pushing for self-reliance ('Aatmanirbhar Bharat') in critical infrastructure technologies, especially after concerns about import dependence on foreign telecom equipment vendors for core network components. C-DOT, DoT's premier R&D arm established in 1984, has historically developed indigenous switching and telecom technologies and more recently has worked on 4G/5G stacks, quantum security, and optical networking. Optical communication technologies (fibre-based core and access networks) underpin the backbone of broadband and 5G/6G infrastructure, and indigenous testbeds help startups validate products before commercial deployment, reducing time-to-market and dependency on foreign testing facilities.

This initiative fits within broader government efforts to build a domestic telecom equipment ecosystem, complementing schemes like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for telecom and networking products, and the Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF). Quantum security integration also signals early alignment with post-quantum cryptography preparedness for critical communication infrastructure, an emerging global concern as quantum computing threatens conventional encryption.
